<description>
Fixes #34714.

Packagers currently need to copy shell completion scripts from `contrib/completions/` into the appropriate system directories. Install the scripts alongside their corresponding binaries with `cmake --install`, including when installing a binary by component.

Targets declare their available bash and fish scripts explicitly, following the existing `HAS_MANPAGE` pattern. This avoids deciding what to install based on file existence at configure time.

Bash scripts install to `${datadir}/bash-completion/completions/`; fish scripts install to `${datadir}/fish/vendor_completions.d/`. Both are enabled by default. Use `-DINSTALL_BASH_COMPLETIONS=OFF` or `-DINSTALL_FISH_COMPLETIONS=OFF` to disable either shell’s scripts.
</description>

[2026-09-21] r:5269307630 review APPROVED by ryanofsky (member):
Code review ACK 91b96bef3465eba2c4710a3b85c77ceb5809e142. Since last review this was updated to stop checking for file existence at configure time, and instead require `install_binary_component` callers to explicitly specify which completions exist. The `INSTALL_COMPLETIONS` configure option added by the previous version is also replaced now with separate `INSTALL_BASH_COMPLETIONS` and `INSTALL_FISH_COMPLETIONS` options now.

(I do agree with purpleKarrot https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34721#issuecomment-4030028919 it would be better to use install components and not have these options. Ideally cmake should control how things are built, not what things are built or installed or tested. It's nice to be able to run cmake once and then forget about it, using your preferred build system, IDE, or command line tools after that and not needing to interact with cmake again just to build and test different targets. But this isn't how bitcoin core build works right now, so this PR is right to follow existing patterns.)
</new_statements>
